sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- lens_diagnostics: lens_diagnostics source=session reads the session cache and an empty cache is not proof of a clean file; use source=lsp scope=paths for changed files when cached findings are absent or stale
- symbol_search: Find files by identifier
- effective_config: Explain resolved configuration
- project_report: Orient in a project before choosing a file
- module_report: Outline a source module before reading a body
- read_symbol: Read one symbol's body instead of the whole file
- read_enclosing: Read the enclosing symbol or callback body for a line
- pi_lens_activate_tools: Activate a situational tool
- subagent_gate: Run subagent tasks with bounded retries and a required success quorum
- workspace_session_summaries: Inspect same-CWD session summaries before potentially overlapping repository work
- subagent: Delegate focused work to child agents; compose multi-child work in one workflow call.
- subagents_enable: pi-subagents is installed. For authorized specialist, independent-review, or parallel work, call subagents_enable, then subagent. Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.
- ask_user_question: Ask the user up to 4 structured questions (2-4 options each) when requirements are ambiguous
- workflow: Delegate substantive independent or staged work to subagents with a JavaScript workflow, optionally composing agent calls with parallel(), pipeline(), or both
- workflow_control: Inspect and manage workflow runs directly by canonical run ID.

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use subagent_gate instead of raw subagent calls when a delegated result must be retried safely or a success quorum must be enforced.
- Set each subagent_gate task retrySafety to read-only only when rerunning it cannot duplicate file mutations or external side effects; omission defaults to may-write.
- Use workspace_session_summaries when another Pi session in the same working directory may overlap the current work.
- After workspace_session_summaries, compare goals, files or symbols, decisions, and next steps; when overlap is material or ownership is unclear, coordinate through intercom before writing.
- Use ask_user_question whenever the user's request is underspecified and you cannot proceed without concrete decisions — you can ask up to 4 questions per invocation.
- Each question MUST have 2-4 options. Every option requires a concise label (1-5 words) and a description explaining what the choice means or its trade-offs. The user can additionally type a custom answer via the automatically appended "Type something." row on every question, or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author "Other" or "Type something." labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.
- Set multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. Provide an options[].preview markdown string when an option benefits from richer side-by-side context (mockups, code snippets, diagrams, configs) — single-select only. The "Type something." row is appended to every question; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column. If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option and append "(Recommended)" to its label.
- Do not stack multiple ask_user_question calls back-to-back — group all clarifying questions into one invocation.
- The `workflow` tool runs multi-agent orchestration — it fans decomposable work out across subagents, and fits tasks shaped like: repo-wide inspection, independent parallel research/checks, multi-perspective review, or fan-out/fan-in synthesis. ONLY call it when the user explicitly opts in — via the workflow trigger word, `/workflows run`, or their own words (e.g. 'run a workflow', 'fan this out', '并行审一遍'). For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit — do not call it; you may briefly offer it (with a rough cost) as an option instead.
- Use workflow_control for workflow lifecycle management; do not ask the user to type /workflows when this tool can perform the action.
- Use stop to terminate or quit a run. Closing the navigator does not stop a run.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.description: Run a JavaScript workflow that delegates work to subagents with agent(), optionally composing calls with parallel() and pipeline().

Add phases: [{ title: 'Phase' }] only when the workflow has named phases, and declare only phases it will use. With multiple phases, call phase('Exact Title') before each phase's work or set `phase` in the agent options. Use `await workflow(savedName, childArgs)` to run a saved workflow inline; nesting is limited to one level and shares the parent run's concurrency, agent, and token limits. Optional quality helpers include verify(), judgePanel(), loopUntilDry(), and completenessCheck(). Optional control helpers include retry() and gate(); budget exposes total, spent(), and remaining(), and phase('Name', { budget: N }) sets a phase token limit. The optional `agentType` option selects a named user or project definition that can bind tools, a model, and role instructions; use it only when its name and purpose are provided in context. Its bound model overrides `tier`; an explicit `model` overrides both. Use plain JavaScript only; imports, require(), filesystem modules, Date.now(), Math.random(), and new Date() are unavailable. Use phase('Name'), agent(prompt, opts), parallel(arrayOfFunctions), pipeline(items, ...stages), log(message), args, cwd, process.cwd(), and budget. The workflow must call agent() at least once. parallel() requires functions, not promises, and returns results in input order: await parallel(items.map(item => () => agent(...))). pipeline(items, ...stages) runs stages sequentially for each item while items proceed concurrently; each stage receives (previousValue, originalItem, index).

# LogViewer — Unified Flexible Log Viewer

All four log surfaces render through one presentational component:

- task Logs tab (`tasks/LogsPanel.jsx`)
- monitor live console, desktop and compact/mobile (`observability/widgets/LiveConsoleWidget.jsx`, used by `ObservabilityDashboard.jsx` and `MobileMonitorView.jsx`)
- orchestrator activity console (`workflow/ActivityConsole.jsx`)

Capture, processing, and persistence are unchanged: the viewer only dresses
records that already exist. Monitoring headers, status pills, the task status
bar, the stuck check, agent messages, and tool cards all stay owned by their
surfaces — only the log body is unified.

## Files

- `frontend/src/components/logs/LogViewer.jsx` — presentational only. No data
  fetching, no context coupling. Props: `records`, optional pre-grouped
  `groups` (or `groupMode: 'turn' | 'source' | 'none'`), `viewer` state,
  `header`/`footer` slots, `onCopy`/`onClear`, `copiedLogs`,
  `showCopyButton`, `scrollKey`, `emptyMessage`, `searchLabel`,
  `logLabel`, `testId`, `fullTextById`.
- `frontend/src/components/logs/logViewerState.js` — `useLogViewerState({ surface, taskId })`
  owns categories, search, density, timestamp visibility/format, auto-scroll,
  and expanded rows. Pure initializers `initialCategories` / `initialSearch`
  are exported for tests.
- `frontend/src/components/logs/logCategories.js` — pure taxonomy:
  classification, normalization, filtering, grouping, timestamps,
  intervention, repeat flagging, legacy migration, chip counts, copy format.
- `frontend/src/components/logs/adapters.js` — `adaptTaskEntry(s)`,
  `adaptProcessLogLine(s)`, and the named dedup policy
  `excludeToolMirrorLinesWhenToolCardsShown`.
- `frontend/src/components/logs/__fixtures__.js` — real-shaped golden inputs.

## LogRecord shape

```ts
type LogRecord = {
  id: string;                 // source id, else deterministic `log-rec-N`
  ts: string | null;          // passed through, never invented
  category: LogCategory;      // primary lane (see below)
  secondaryCategories: LogCategory[]; // cross-cutting lanes (matching counts)
  tag: string;                // display tag, e.g. `[TOOL]` (derived from kind when absent)
  title?: string | null;
  text: string;
  detail?: string | null;     // expansion payload (tool output, usage JSON, raw source)
  meta?: Record<string, unknown> | null; // live lines stash `meta.rawLine` (by reference)
  kind?: string | null;
  collapsedThinking: boolean;
  fullTextId?: string | number | null;
  turn: number | null;
  source: 'task' | 'process-live' | ...;
  projectName?: string | null;
  taskId?: string | null;
  projectId?: string | null;
  isIntervention: boolean;
  isRepeated: boolean;
};
```

## Category taxonomy

`output`, `tools`, `thinking`, `ci`, `stage`, `debug`, `system`, `human`,
`error`, `git`, `raw`. Classification is tag-first with text fallback so
structured entries (`kind`) and live lines (`tag`/`text` only) converge:

1. Structured `kind` wins (`thinking`/`tool`/`assistant`/`error`/
   `telemetry`→`raw`/`permission`→`human`/`plan`→`stage`).
2. Live lines dispatch on `tag` (`[TOOL]`→tools, `[CI]`/`[CI/CMD]`→ci,
   `[GIT]`→git, `[HUMAN]`→human, `[DEBUG]`/`[TRACE]`/`[VERBOSE]`→debug,
   `[USAGE]`/`[RAW]`→raw, `[PERM]`→human, `[PLAN]`→stage, `[AGENT]`→output,
   `[INFO]`/`[SYSTEM]`/`[WARN]`→system), with `text`-prefix fallback.
3. Content patterns: `STAGE_FAILBACK`/failback → `stage` (wins over generic
   tags); KainBain debug markers → `debug` (wins over generic tags);
   `STAGE_*`/stage-movement phrasing → `stage`; checkpoint/approval phrasing
   → `human`; timeout/nonzero-exit/failure phrasing → `error`.
4. CI stream wrappers: `[STDOUT]\n…` and `[STDERR]\n…` prefixes (emitted by
   `api/flow/commandStages.js` when capturing stage stdout/stderr) are
   unwrapped before classification — `[STDERR]` lines classify as `error`,
   and the content line's tag classifies `[STDOUT]` output. The same grammar
   applies in `api/watch/processLogs.js::_logEntryKindFromText` (backend)
   and `tasks/logEntryModel.js::entryFromLogLine` (legacy parse).
5. `[INFO] Task initialized…` placeholders are always `system`.
6. Untagged live stdout reads as `output`; unknown structured entries stay
   `system`.

Secondary lanes: collapsed thinking markers carry `output` (visible in the
default narrative); full thinking blocks are primary-only `thinking`.
Failure text on a non-error primary adds `error`; checkpoint text on a
non-human primary adds `human`.

## Filter semantics

- Multi-select chips; `All` resets to density defaults. Empty selection (or
  `ALL`) shows everything. Primary **or** secondary membership counts.
- Search ANDs with chips over text + tag + title, case-insensitive.
- Defaults exclude `thinking` (full blocks only — markers ride along),
  `debug`, and `raw` until opted in. This reproduces the legacy ALL narrative
  exactly while making every lane a user choice.
- Repeat flagging (`markRepeated`, window of 8) marks identical
  category/tag/text rows without dropping them.

## Density and timestamps

- **Compact**: tight rows, tag pill, optional short timestamp, wrapping body.
  Default for monitor/activity surfaces.
- **Full**: roomier rows plus a metadata line (turn/task/repeat). Default for
  task logs.
- Any row with `detail` (or a resolvable thinking marker via `fullTextById`)
  expands inline through a button with `aria-expanded`.
- Timestamps render when enabled: on by default in full, off in compact.
  Formats `HH:MM:SS`, `HH:MM:SS.mmm`, `ISO`. Short clock times pass through;
  missing/invalid stamps render `—` — fake times are never invented.

## Intervention summary

`interventionSummary` counts **Errors** (error lane, ERROR/FAIL/STDERR tags,
`[ERROR]`/`[FAIL]`/`[STDERR]` text patterns including behind stream wrappers,
failure text), **Checkpoints** (human lane), and **Repeated** rows. Any
errors/checkpoints raise the **Needs attention** badge; rows highlight with a
tint plus a screen-reader marker (color is never the only signal). Nothing is
auto-hidden.

## Persistence keys and migration

- Task: `kainbain:logViewer:task:<taskId>:{categories,search,density,timestamps,timestampFormat,autoScroll}`
- Live: `kainbain:logViewer:live:{…}` · Activity: `kainbain:logViewer:activity:{…}`
- Expanded rows are session-only (never persisted).
- One-way read-only migration, applied only when no unified key exists:
  - `kainbain:taskLogs:<id>:feed` → categories (`TOOLS`→tools, …; unknown→defaults)
  - `kainbain:taskLogs:<id>:search` → search
  - `kainbain:board:logTag` → categories (`ERROR`→error, `CI/CMD`→ci, …)
  - `kainbain:board:logSearch` → search
- Stale legacy keys are left untouched. Corrupt values fall back to density
  defaults (categories) or `''` (search).

## Compatibility facades

- `tasks/logEntryModel.js` is the normalization seam only
  (`normalizeEntries`, `fullTextIndex`, plus the legacy text parse): the task
  hook still computes legacy entries for the marker-safe copy path, and
  existing unit tests pin the model. Grouping, filtering, search, severity,
  and detail expansion live in the viewer (`logCategories`, `adapters`).
- `workflow/nodeModel.js :: filterProcessLogs` is reimplemented over the new
  taxonomy (legacy tag → categories, `[TOOL]` mirrors dropped) but returns
  the ORIGINAL line objects, so copy formatting is byte-identical. It also
  re-exports `excludeToolMirrorLinesWhenToolCardsShown`.
- `severityTagStyle` / `severityTextClass` remain for existing tests; the
  viewer uses its own category pill tones.

## Accessibility

- Scroll regions: `role="log"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="false"`,
  `tabIndex={0}`.
- Chips and density/timestamp toggles: `aria-pressed`; empty lanes disabled
  but visible with `(0)` counts.
- Expansions are buttons with `aria-expanded` and stable labels
  (`Show thinking (N chars)`, `Show full detail`).
- Auto-scroll degrades for reduced-motion users via
  `scrollIntoViewRespectingMotion`.

## Test map

- `logs/logCategories.test.js` — taxonomy matrix, secondaries, filter
  composition, grouping, timestamps, intervention, repeats, migration.
- `logs/adapters.test.js` — adapter equivalence, raw-line stash, dedup policy.
- `logs/LogViewer.test.jsx` — chips/counts/aria, multi-select, search,
  density, timestamps, expansion, copy, intervention strip, groups, reset.
- `logs/logViewerState.test.js` — defaults, round-trip, invalid data, legacy
  migration, per-task isolation.
- Migrated: `tasks/LogsPanel.test.jsx`, `tasks/TaskDetailOverlay.test.jsx`,
  `observability/*`, `workflow/ActivityConsole.test.jsx`,
  `workflow/WorkflowCanvas.console.test.jsx`, `workflow/nodeModel.test.js`
  (facade + policy re-export), `canary-e2e/tests/task-logs.spec.js`.

# Unified Logging Platform

This document describes the unified log platform introduced for all harnesses
in the `kb/699d3c28-8f09-4fce-bd4b-c368406aa88b` task. The goal is that no
harness silently drops meaningful output, and that `task.logEntries` reads
like (or better than) running the harness CLI, with Pi as the gold standard.

## Canonical log record

Entries keep the legacy shape `{ id, ts, feed, feeds, kind, turn, text, meta }`
and gain optional typed fields at read/processor time:

- `seq`, `blockId`, `runId`, `harnessId`, `model`
- `fidelity`: `exact` | `normalized` | `synthesized`
- `evidence`: `{ wireType, sourceEvent, reason? }` (bounded raw lane)
- `tool`: `{ callId, name, args, result, exitCode, durationMs, partials }`
- `usage`: `{ inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedTokens, totalTokens, costUsd, contextUsed, contextWindow, steps, tokensPerSecond, model }`

New kinds: `assistant | thinking | tool | error | system | telemetry |
permission | plan | raw`. New feeds: `main | thinking | tools | telemetry |
raw`.

## Processing layer

- `api/agent/logStream/logRecord.js` — pure record factory and normalizer.
- `api/agent/logStream/logProcessor.js` — the only place normalized events
  become canonical records; `agentLogStreamer.js` is a thin state shell over
  it.

## Normalized event vocabulary (additive)

Added to `api/agent/sessionEvents.js` alongside the original 8 names:

- `usage_updated` `{ usage, model? }`
- `session_meta` `{ model?, effort?, sandbox?, permissions?, conversationId?, runFacts? }`
- `permission_requested` / `permission_resolved` `{ method?, target?, decision? }`
- `plan_updated` `{ steps[] }`
- `reasoning_delta` `{ delta }`
- `harness_log` `{ text, tag? }`

Original 8 names remain unchanged so old sessions stay valid.

## Limits (config)

- `logEntriesMaxCount` (default 500) total bound.
- `telemetryMaxCount` (default 100) reserved telemetry budget.
- `rawMaxCount` (default 50) raw lane bound.
- `rawMaxBytes` (default 8192) per-record raw source cap.
- `toolArgsMaxLength` 400 / `resultMaxLength` 600; full output in `tool.result`.

## Raw evidence lane

Unmapped or unknown wire events are emitted as `kind: "raw"` records with
`evidence.reason = "unmapped"`, scrubbed for obvious bearer/token patterns and
capped. Harnesses no longer silently drop them.

## Fidelity gate

`api/agent/logStream/harnessFidelity.test.js` asserts per harness that a
recorded fixture run produces records for every advertised capability (text,
thinking/reasoning, tool, telemetry, system/permission/plan) and that known
wire shapes never land in the raw lane as unmapped.

## Per-harness notes

- pi: usage/stop reason recovered from assistant message payloads.
- opencode: token telemetry + permission audit.
- vibe: reasoning rows → thinking; export telemetry structured.
- antigravity: user input/checkpoints surfaced, result usage telemetry.
- muse: reasoning + task/runtime lifecycle; task/terminal records as system.
- custom: stderr → error; exit codes; stdout via harness_log.
- mock: full-lane coverage for tests.

## Limits / design notes

Reasoning stays collapsed by default (`[THINKING] (N chars)`); telemetry
never leaks into narrative/copy except its own feed.

`normalizeRecord` (`api/agent/logStream/logRecord.js`) is exported and unit
tested as the read-time upgrade helper for legacy entries, but no serve path
calls it yet: today's readers (watch routes via `renderLogEntriesText`, the
frontend `logEntryModel`) already tolerate missing `feeds`/`fidelity`, so
wiring it in would change API response shapes for zero reader benefit. The
upcoming visual refactor is the consumer that should adopt it.

Code rule (kept here, not in `agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md`, because that
file is a byte-identical vendored copy whose header forbids in-repo edits):
extend `shared/toolLogFormat.js` for new render summaries, never fork a
parallel renderer; route unmapped data to the bounded raw lane, never a silent
`default:` drop.

## Failure modes (how this layer can fail, and what happens)

- **Unknown event type** → `kind: "raw"` record on the `raw` feed with
  `evidence.reason = "unmapped"` (scrubbed, capped at `rawMaxBytes`). Never a
  crash, never silent. Raw-lane overflow evicts oldest-first under one
  updating `[INFO] (N earlier raw entries evicted)` marker on the raw feed.
- **Malformed event (null, non-object, missing/non-string `type`)** → ignored,
  `handleEvent` returns `[]`. There is no wire type to attribute, so there is
  nothing honest to record.
- **Hostile `makeLogRecord` input (null, array, array `meta`, bad `turn`,
  unknown `fidelity`)** → degrades to defaults (system kind, main feed,
  turn 1, `{}` meta, kind-derived fidelity). Never throws.
- **Unserializable/circular wire payload** → `boundRawSource` falls back from
  `JSON.stringify` to `String()` to `"[unserializable wire event]"`. Never
  throws, never stores an empty source for a real payload.
- **Total overflow (`logEntriesMaxCount`)** → oldest entries evicted under one
  updating `[INFO] (N earlier log entries evicted)` marker that always stays
  first; the marker itself is exempt from eviction. Telemetry keeps a reserved
  budget (`telemetryMaxCount`) so a narrative flood cannot starve usage
  records; duplicate usage payloads are suppressed via payload dedupe.
- **Unknown feed/kind/fidelity strings** → fall back to `main`/`system`/
  kind-derived fidelity. Unknown `consumeFeed`/`GET /logs` feed → loud 400/
  throw (fail-loud at the API boundary, fail-safe inside the pipeline).
- **Secrets in wire payloads** → already redacted at the child-env seam
  (`harnessScaffold.buildChildEnv`); the raw lane additionally scrubs
  bearer/api-key shapes as defense in depth. Raw bytes stay in
  `evidence.sourceEvent`, never in display `text` (which is also ANSI
  stripped).

## Operations (transfer and continuation)

- **Config-first tuning:** lane budgets are config keys
  (`logEntriesMaxCount`, `telemetryMaxCount`, `rawMaxCount`, `rawMaxBytes`;
  see `api/config/schema.js`), so operators retune without code changes.
  Missing/invalid values fall back to compiled defaults in
  `createLogProcessor` — an unset key never unbounds a lane (`rawMaxBytes: 0`
  means the default cap, not uncapped).
- **Rolling upgrades:** records are additive — old tasks without the new
  fields render exactly as before, and new code reads old entries without
  migration (storage is never rewritten).
- **Two surfaces during transition:** harness-internal `harness.log` lines
  still reach project process logs while also becoming structured entries, so
  existing process-log tailing keeps working.
- **Rollback:** each harness mapper migration reverts independently — the
  processor tolerates the absence of new events, and unknown future wire
  shapes land in the raw lane instead of breaking the run.

Cross-reference: `#/docs/activity-stream`.

## Viewing the lanes

Structured kinds map to viewer lanes in [LogViewer.md](LogViewer.md):
`assistant`→Direct output, `tool`→Tool calls, `thinking`→Thinking traces
(markers stay narrative-visible; full blocks need the lane), `error`→Errors,
`telemetry`/`raw`→Telemetry/raw (opt-in), `permission`→Human/checkpoints,
`plan`→Stage movement, and `system` splits by tag/text into CI/Git/Human/
Stage/Debug/System. Until the telemetry/raw collection lands, those lanes
simply stay empty and disabled.

# Values

## User understandable over technical language

I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible

### Principles

- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
- File structure should reflect the call stack
- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
- Include why things are done not just what is done
- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
  
  

## Functional over Object oreintated

Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).

### Principles

- Try and avoid using classes where possible
- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility


## Co-location over abstraction

Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.

### Principles
- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
- Don’t fear repetition of code
- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
- Use folders as a tool for organising

## Tested over trusted 

Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 

### Principles
- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
- Tests must be consistent
- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle


## Fast iteration over long planning

Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.

### Principles
- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
